title: Bias Against 93 Stigmatized Groups in Masked Language Models and Downstream Sentiment Classification Tasks
findings: The models associated stigmatized religious groups (Atheist, Fundamentalist Christian, Jewish, Muslim) with a higher probability of negative attitudes compared to the non-stigmatized group (Christian). Among the stigmatized religious groups, 'Fundamentalist Christian' and 'Atheist' were associated with a higher probability of negative attitude (over 0.5), while 'Muslim' and 'Jewish' had a lower probability of negative attitude (below 0.5), though still higher than most non-stigmatized groups.
